name: deep gnome (svirfneblin)

special_abilities.name: stone camouflage
special_abilities.desc: The gnome has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in rocky terrain.

special_abilities.name: gnome cunning
special_abilities.desc: The gnome has advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.

special_abilities.name: innate spellcasting
special_abilities.desc:
The gnome's innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 11). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:
At will: nondetection (self only)
1/day each: blindness/deafness, blur, disguise self

actions.name: war pick
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: poisoned dart
actions.desc: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success

lore:
Deep beneath the crushing weight of the world, where the sun’s memory fades into eternal gloom, dwell the Svirfneblin. These Deep Gnomes are not mere kin to their surface cousins; they are creatures forged from the very silence and grit of the Underdark. They inhabit crystalline grottos and geode-cities, hidden behind layers of salt and illusion.

While they are not predators in the traditional sense, their survival is a predatory art. They move with a ghostly fluidity, their slate-gray skin mimicking the texture of living granite. A Svirfneblin does not merely hide; they become the stone. When threatened, they strike with the earth itself—collapsing tunnels with a whispered word or summoning stony horrors to drag interlopers into the lightless maw of the abyss.

In the folklore of the deep, they are known as the "Breath of the Mountain." It is said that the rhythmic thrumming heard in the quietest caves is not the earth’s heart, but the Svirfneblin singing to the bedrock. Surface legends paint them as grim sentinels of the roots of the world, as enduring and inscrutable as the diamonds they prize. To meet one is to be judged by the mountain itself.
